input.brief: SAS3D: a three-person remote freelance product team (design, development, DevOps) shipping fixed-price web products for early-stage companies; own case-study screenshots and team portraits

direction.name: The contact sheet
direction.idea: Show everything at once, small, in order. The work is laid out like a photographer's contact sheet or an archive drawer: dozens of small frames in strict rows, with all text set at one small size. Nothing is featured, which is the point: the volume and consistency of the body of work is the statement, and the visitor does the choosing. It suits people and studios whose strength is range and output.
direction.composition: The name, or one sentence about the work, sits at display size (6–9vw) across the top of the first screen, and the sheet begins directly under it, still inside the first screen. The first screen opens with three or four short blocks of small text across the top on a 12-column grid (who, what, where to reach them), all at 14–16px, and immediately below, the sheet begins: rows of thumbnails at a fixed height (90–140px) with their natural widths, 6–10px gaps, each project forming a run of four to eight frames preceded by its title in the same small text. The sheet fills the whole page width edge to edge with 16–20px margins. Hovering a run dims the others and shows that project's one-line description in a fixed position. A single enlarged frame may interrupt the sheet once per screen at four times the size.
direction.typography: One face. The name at display size on the first screen; everything else at one text size and one small size; hierarchy below the name comes from position and from a single brighter ink for titles.
direction.colour: Black or white ground, so the thumbnails are the only colour.
direction.imagery: Many images: at least 24 frames to make a sheet. They can be project photographs from the dealt set cropped to mixed ratios, or page captures of the work. Square corners, no captions on the frames.
direction.richness: Density and order. The mass of small images forms a texture; the strict rows keep it calm.
direction.pitfalls: With fewer than about 20 images it looks unfinished; choose another direction. Do not add a big headline above the sheet. On a phone the frames become two per row at a fixed height and each run scrolls sideways. Rows that run past the right edge read as clipped in screenshots and to most visitors: wrap the frames onto the next line, or end each row inside the grid.

hero.name: Ring of frames around the headline
hero.blueprint: One near-black or deep flat field. Eighteen to twenty-four photographs or film stills sit on an ellipse centred on the viewport, with radii of 560px across and 310px down, so their centres run from x 160 to 1280 and from y 140 to 760. Frames have square corners and no border, mix 4:3 and 3:4, and grow towards the viewer: about 100px wide at the top of the ring and 150px at the bottom and at both ends, so the ring reads as tilted. Each frame is turned so its base lies along the curve (never more than 30 degrees), and neighbours may overlap by up to a fifth. Inside the ring an empty core about 600×340px holds the text, centred: the headline on two lines at clamp(56px, 5.4vw, 80px), leading 0.95, in the light ink; one supporting sentence at 18px, max 40ch, 24px under it; then the single action as a solid light rectangle. Wordmark top-left and three text links top-right at 15px on 32px margins, outside the ring. Every frame is a link to its project: pointing at one, or focusing it, brings it to full brightness, drops the others to 45% and replaces the supporting sentence with that project's name and year. Place the frames with a few lines of trigonometry (left and top in percentages) and keep them still; the wheel scrolls the page as usual.
hero.mobile: The ellipse becomes a circle 132vw across, centred at half height, so the frames at its left and right ends run off both edges and the ring reads as two arcs, one above and one below the text. Keep twelve frames at 64–88px. The headline sits in the core at 10.5vw on two lines inside 28px margins, with the sentence at 16px and the action at the full width of the core beneath it. Wordmark top-left and a menu word top-right sit above the top arc. A tap on a frame opens its project.
hero.headline: A 3–6 word line on two lines, at most about 14 characters per line, so it fits the empty core.

type.note: A light grotesque with open, slightly old-fashioned shapes; large headings look airy and the text weight beneath stays easy to read. Suits AI and research products, fashion houses and calm brand sites.

palette.name: Plum-black and pink
palette.note: Near-black and plum at the top and bottom bracket a white middle with navy-black text. Hot pink is reserved for primary buttons, bars in charts and map markers; it never fills a section.

motion.name: Masked headline
motion.description: On load, each line of the headline rises from behind its own baseline, about 900ms with a strong ease-out, the second line 110ms after the first; the supporting sentence and the action then fade up together. Nothing else on the page performs. Because headlines are two lines at most, you author the line breaks and wrap each line yourself. Recipe: 'Masked line reveal' in references/motion.md.

sections.name: One strip per project
sections.blueprint: The left 13% of the width is a `position: sticky` column holding the section name at 28px and, beneath it, two text filters at 15px, the active one in full ink. To its right each project is one horizontal strip of four to six images, all exactly 190px tall at their natural widths (`height: 190px; width: auto`), 8px apart, the last one cut off by the right viewport edge with `overflow: hidden`. Under each strip, one line at 13px spread across the strip's width: project name flush left, a three-word descriptor at the centre, the year flush right. 45px separate one strip from the next, so four projects fit on a 900px screen and ten make a page. Square corners; no captions on individual frames. Hovering a strip dims the other strips to 40% opacity. There is no heading beyond the section name in the rail.
sections.mobile: The rail becomes a single line above the list: section name left, filters right. Strips are 120px tall and each scrolls sideways on its own with `overflow-x: auto` and scroll snapping. The caption line keeps the name left and the year right; the descriptor is dropped.

sections.name: Side facts, wide paragraph
sections.blueprint: Two rows share one vertical line at 34% of the viewport width. Row one: in a 160px column at the left margin, three label and value pairs stack with 20px between them, each a label in the soft ink with its value beneath in full ink, all at 13px (founded, based in, team size). From the 34% line a five-line paragraph at clamp(20px, 1.7vw, 26px), leading 1.35, runs to 90% of the width. Row two starts 120px lower and repeats the logic for the record of the practice: one plain word at 13px at the far left (awards, press, clients), then from the 34% line two list columns, each 260px wide with a 64px gutter, at 13px with 10px between lines: name at the left, year at the right in the soft ink. No heading; the paragraph opens the section. Each list comfortably holds 6–12 lines. No photographs are needed.
sections.mobile: Everything aligns to the left margin. The paragraph comes first at 19px. The three label and value pairs follow as a two-column grid at 14px. The two record lists stack with 40px between them, each opened by its plain word in full ink.

sections.name: One-size name columns
sections.blueprint: Pure text at one size. Three columns start on columns 1, 4 and 7 of the 12-column grid, leaving columns 10–12 empty on purpose. Each column opens with a group name in full ink and continues with a tight stack of six to ten capability names in the soft ink, all at 16–17px, regular weight, line-height 1.25, no bullets and no symbols; one blank line separates group name from stack. Hovering a name brings it to full ink and shows a one-line description in a fixed spot: the top of the empty columns 10–12, at the same size. The heading is no larger than 28px; two or three words, alone on column 1, 96px above the columns. Give the section 20vh of empty ground above and below, so the smallness reads as decided. Works on light or deep grounds.
sections.mobile: Columns stack with 40px between groups; text rises to 18px with line-height 1.4 for touch. Group names stay in full ink. Hover descriptions are dropped; each group ends instead with one sentence in the soft ink that sums it up. The heading is 24px, 48px above.

sections.name: Drag row of moments
sections.blueprint: A story told left to right. Top row: the heading, two to four words at 28–36px, at the left margin; at the right margin two solid square buttons, 48px each, for back and forward. Directly beneath, a solid bar 6px tall spans the full width in a soft tone, with a full-ink segment showing how far the row has been scrolled. Then the row itself: six to nine columns, each 280px wide with 32px gaps, in a horizontally scrolling flex container with scroll-snap that bleeds off both viewport edges. Every column reads top to bottom: a one-line caption at 18px bold that carries the order in words ('We met', 'Two winters on', 'The move'), three lines at 15px in the soft ink, then 80–140px of empty space that varies per column, then a 4:5 portrait photograph. Because the spaces vary, the photographs' top edges rise and fall along the row.
sections.mobile: Columns are 72vw wide with 16px gaps, so the next one always shows at the right edge. The buttons are dropped; the 6px progress bar stays under the heading. The empty space inside columns shrinks to 32–64px but still varies from column to column.

sections.name: Lead quote, corner quotes
sections.blueprint: A single field one viewport tall (min-height 100svh), usually the darkest tone of the palette. The lead quotation sits in the upper third: two lines at about 4vw in a light weight, centred, no wider than 60% of the viewport, with nothing near it. Two further short quotations are pushed into the bottom-left and bottom-right corners, each a block three columns wide set at 16px with leading 1.5, left-aligned, with the speaker's name and role on the two lines beneath in the softer ink. The bottom centre, about six columns wide, is deliberately empty. Use a three-row grid (auto 1fr auto) so the corner blocks hold a bottom margin of 32px while the lead quotation keeps its place at any height. There is no heading and there are no portraits; the contrast between one large voice and two small ones is the composition.
sections.mobile: The lead quotation moves to the top at 8vw over three or four lines, left-aligned, with 96px of empty field under it. The two small quotations then stack at 16px, the first full width, the second indented by a quarter of the screen so they do not read as a list.

sections.name: Plan names, one live figure
sections.blueprint: Plans are a list of names; the price shown belongs to whichever name is selected. Columns 1–6 hold the plan names stacked at about 5vw, leading 1.1, each a `<button>`; the selected one is in the full ink, the others in the softer ink, and the selected name carries a solid dot 0.3em across at its left. Columns 8–12 hold one stage that stays in place while its contents change: the selected plan's price at about 9vw at the top, the period beside it at 18px, a paragraph of three or four lines at 18px saying what that plan includes, and one rectangular button whose label names the plan. Changing plan swaps the stage contents with a 200ms crossfade; the figure's position never moves. Selection follows click and keyboard focus. The middle plan is selected on load. There is no heading: the names are the heading.
sections.mobile: Plan names stack at 10vw, each on its own line. Tapping one opens its stage directly beneath that name (price at 20vw, paragraph at 17px, full-width button) and closes the others, like a large accordion without lines. The middle plan starts open.

sections.name: Answers as reading text
sections.blueprint: The questions and answers are set as continuous reading text, like the notes at the back of a programme. A heading of two or three words at 28–32px sits in columns 1–3, top-aligned. Columns 5–12 hold the text in two columns (`columns: 2; column-gap: 56px`), each about 36ch wide, at 16–17px with leading 1.55. Each item is one paragraph: the question is the opening run-in, set in the medium weight in the full ink and ending with its question mark, and the answer continues on the same line in the regular weight. Paragraphs are separated by 20px and carry `break-inside: avoid` so none splits across columns. No toggles, no icons, no boxes. Eight to fourteen items fit on one screen, which is the point: everything is answered at a glance. Where the page's reading column is narrow, use one column.
sections.mobile: One column at 16px with 20px margins. The heading leads at 24px. Each paragraph keeps its run-in question in the medium weight, with 18px between paragraphs. The section may run to two screens; do not collapse it into an accordion.

sections.name: Three photographs, then a field
sections.blueprint: Two parts with no gap between them. First, a strip of three photographs butted edge to edge across the full viewport, each one third wide and 40svh tall, `object-fit: cover`, no gutters and no captions; give all three the same treatment. Directly beneath, a band in one flat palette colour, about 44svh tall. In the band, columns 1–7: the closing statement at 26–30px over three lines in the band's assigned ink, with exactly one phrase underlined by a 4px bar (`text-decoration-thickness: 4px; text-underline-offset: 6px`), and that phrase is the link; two lines at 16px follow 32px lower. In the lower-right corner, columns 11–12, a small portrait photograph (4:5, about 150px wide) sits 40px from the band's edges: the person who will answer. There is no button; the underlined phrase is the action.
sections.mobile: The strip becomes one full-width photograph at 4:3 with the other two side by side beneath it at half width each, still gutterless. The band follows: statement at 22px, the two small lines, and the portrait at 96px wide in the bottom-right corner.

sections.name: A footer of tiles
sections.blueprint: The footer is the last two rows of a board: filled tiles with 8px gaps and 8–12px outer margins, every cell used. Upper row, each tile 220px tall: a statement tile in columns 1–4 with one sentence at 24px top-left and the legal text at 12px bottom-left; a navigation tile in columns 5–7 with a plain list at 16px; a tile in columns 8–9 giving the city and local time as text; an email tile in columns 10–12 with the address at 20px as a link, bottom-left. Lower row, 320px tall: a tile in the ink colour spanning columns 1–8 with the wordmark set large (about 9vw) and centred, and a tile in the accent colour in columns 9–12 with a two-to-four-word invitation top-left at 28px and an arrow, drawn as inline SVG with 4px strokes, in its bottom-right corner; the whole accent tile is a link.
sections.mobile: Two columns of tiles with 6px gaps: the wordmark tile full width first at 160px tall, the accent tile full width next, then navigation and email side by side, then time and statement. Every tile keeps 20px padding and top-left text.

references.name: Smallbits
references.idea: The icon set is the page: a full-viewport wall of the product with one docked card holding every word.
references.hero: The whole viewport is a black field tiled with white pixel icons, each drawn about 50px on a 112px pitch, nine rows deep; alternate rows shift half a cell so it reads as a brick pattern, and icons at the edges are cropped. There is no header. A white square-cornered card, 795×170px, is docked bottom-centre: a two-line 24px semibold sentence left, a black rectangular button right, a row of five grey links below. A third-party badge floats top-right. This single screen is the entire page.
references.type: Inter 600 at 24px, -0.02em, for the one sentence; Inter 16px semibold grey for links and button. Nothing exceeds 1.7vw — the pixel icons, not type, are the display element.
references.colour: #000000 #ffffff #9a9a9a #ff6154 — Strict black and white: white icons on black, black text on a white card, grey for secondary links. The only colour is the coral third-party badge.
references.imagery: About ninety visible pixel icons, each an 8×8 bitmap drawn at 50px in pure white with hard edges, tiled full-bleed and cropped at the viewport edges.
references.layout: One viewport, no scroll. A staggered icon grid fills the frame edge to edge; all words live in one docked card. On mobile the card becomes a full-width white block with a full-width button.

sections.description: Mobile restack, the only other state. The icon wall drops to five columns filling the top 73% of the screen; the card becomes a full-width white block at the bottom with the sentence on three lines at 18px, a full-width black button 78px tall, and five grey links spaced evenly on one line.

steal: Make the product the wallpaper: tile the full viewport with the assets at large size and skip a hero image entirely.
Offset alternate rows by half a cell so a regular grid reads as a pattern rather than a table.
Compress all copy, the CTA and the footer links into one docked card so the page never needs to scroll.

references.name: PROOOOF
references.idea: The product's output is the page: a wall of photos each wearing its coloured EXIF strip, with all the copy folded into one small floating card.
references.hero: The whole viewport is a six-column masonry of photographs on a warm off-white ground with about 15px gutters, columns offset vertically so rows never line up. Each photo has a flat strip fused to its bottom edge carrying tiny monospaced capture data, every strip a different solid colour (black, red, orange, yellow, violet, green). Dead centre floats a white card about 380px wide and 410px tall with roughly 28px corner radius and a soft shadow. It contains an extended wordmark with chained O's, a two-row accordion with the first row open, an App Store badge and a monospaced line of links. There is no navigation.
references.type: An extended, heavy wordmark with interlocked O's is the only display type. Card text is Wintyr VF at about 14-16px, medium weight for accordion headings. EXIF strips and footer links are monospace at roughly 8-13px. No headline anywhere.
references.colour: #f3eee9 #fafafa #191818 #ff6a2b #f7c531 #5a4fcf — Colour comes from the photographs and the saturated caption strips, one hue per photo. Card and gutters stay off-white; a final panel flips to near-black with grey characters.
references.imagery: Casual travel, food, pet and concert photos in mixed portrait and landscape crops, square corners, ungraded, tiled edge to edge. The page ends on an ASCII-art rendering of a hand holding a camera.
references.layout: Effectively a single screen: the photo wall sits behind a centred card that carries every word. Six columns on desktop, two on mobile where the card widens to nearly full width. The only second scene is a dark, inset ASCII panel.

sections.description: All product copy lives in the centred card as an accordion: a row with heading left and chevron right, a hairline divider, the open panel's four-line paragraph, a centred store badge, another divider, a collapsed second row, then a small monospaced line with a version number and underlined links. The card stays put while the wall remains visible on all four sides.

Each tile is a photo with a data strip attached below: two or three rows of monospaced text, four values spread evenly across the first row, date and time at opposite ends of the second, maker and model on the third. Strip and text colours change per tile, for example yellow on black, black on yellow, white on violet, so a uniform grid looks varied.

The closing panel is a near-black rectangle inset with wide margins and filled edge to edge with rows of grey ASCII characters that resolve into a picture of a hand gripping a camera. One line of tiny monospaced uppercase text sits at the exact centre as the call to action. No button and no logo.

steal: Show the product's output at wall scale as the background and confine all copy to one small card on top of it.
Give every repeated tile its own flat accent colour for the caption strip so a strict grid reads as lively.
Hold the explanatory copy in an accordion inside the hero card so the page needs no scrolling.

references.name: Depo Luxe
references.idea: A film production roster shown as a full-screen reel in which every step is one film with only a quoted italic title, a director and a client, set like credits at body size.
references.hero: Video fills the viewport edge to edge with no scrim beyond the footage's own darkness. All text is white serif at near-body size. A 305px-wide header block sits top-centre: the two words of the name pushed to its left and right edges, an italic one-line descriptor beneath, then five nav links spread across the same width with the current one underlined. Dead centre: the film title in italic with quotation marks at 40px (under 3% of viewport width), the director's name 60px below. The client name stands alone at the right edge on the title's line. A roman numeral above a thin vertical line marks the left edge.
references.type: EB Garamond only, regular and italic, always white. The largest text on the page is the 40px italic title; names and nav are about 17px. Two sizes, no capitals, no bold, slight negative tracking; the wordmark is simply two words set far apart.
references.colour: #070c0b #081514 #16120d #1f3fd6 #f0f0f0 — Black ground; all colour comes from the footage: teal-black interiors, blue-tinted lenses, one saturated cobalt frame. Type stays white throughout, with no accent colour or UI tint.
references.imagery: Full-bleed commercial film footage: tight faces, extreme close-ups, underwater shots, heavy cinema grade and grain. One per screen, never framed or rounded, with text laid directly on top.
references.layout: One screen equals one project: no margins, cards or grid. Three fixed text anchors repeat on every screen (centre title, right-edge client, left-edge numeral) so only the footage changes. The page is a single viewport that swaps its contents.

sections.description: Each project is a full-viewport slide that keeps the hero's three anchors: quoted italic title dead centre with the director beneath, client name hard against the right edge at the same height, and a roman numeral on the left edge that moves down a thin vertical track as you advance, doubling as progress indicator. Between slides the frame goes fully black with the next title already in place before its footage fades in.

The header is a compact credit block rather than a bar: a fixed column about a fifth of the viewport wide, centred at the top, holding three justified lines (name split to both ends, italic descriptor, five links). It has no background and stays over the footage on every slide. On mobile the same block widens to the text column and the client name moves above the title.

steal: Keep every piece of text at body size over full-bleed footage and let position alone (dead centre, right edge, left edge) create the hierarchy.
Build the header as a narrow centred block of three justified lines, with the two-word name pushed to opposite ends of the first line.
Use a roman numeral sliding along a thin vertical edge line as both project index and scroll progress.
